updates.excerpt: I interned at Thornton Tomasetti's San Francisco office within their structural design, forensics and renewal group from June 02, 2025 to August 22, 2025.
updates.detail: I interned at Thornton Tomasetti's San Francisco office within their structural design, forensics and renewal group from June 02, 2025 to August 22, 2025.

updates.title: 2nd Place in ASCE EMI Conference's Structural Stability Student Paper Competition
updates.excerpt: I attended the American Society of Civil Engineers’ (ASCE) Engineering Mechanics Institute (EMI) conference in Anaheim, California, from May 27 to May 30, 2025, where I presented my paper and gave a talk on “Force-stable reconfigurable truss structures using quadrilateral linkage principles.”
updates.detail:
I attended the American Society of Civil Engineers’ (ASCE) Engineering Mechanics Institute (EMI) conference in Anaheim, California, from May 27 to May 30, 2025. I presented my paper, “Force-stable reconfigurable truss structures using quadrilateral linkage principles,” in the Structural Stability student paper competition and earned second place.

This work showcases a workflow for creating deployable truss systems that remain force-stable through large configuration changes, coupling geometric insight with rigorous structural analysis.

updates.title: Rackham Doctoral Intern Fellowship
updates.excerpt: I received the Rackham Doctoral Internship Fellowship to support my internship at Thornton Tomasetti during Summer 2025.
updates.detail: I received the Rackham Doctoral Internship Fellowship to support my internship at Thornton Tomasetti during Summer 2025. The fellowship enables me to explore career pathways outside academia while applying my research expertise in industry.

updates.title: Research article in the Journal of Fluids and Structures
updates.excerpt: My paper “Rapidly deployable hulls and on-demand tunable hydrodynamics with shape morphed curved crease origami,” co-authored with K. J. Maki and E. T. Filipov, has been published in the Journal of Fluids and Structures.
updates.detail: My paper “Rapidly deployable hulls and on-demand tunable hydrodynamics with shape morphed curved crease origami,” co-authored with K. J. Maki and E. T. Filipov, was published in the Journal of Fluids and Structures. The article demonstrates how origami-inspired morphing surfaces can be used to tune hydrodynamic performance on demand.

updates.title: Dissertation Proposal Exam
updates.excerpt: I defended my dissertation proposal on “Transforming Optimized Static Trusses into Shape-morphing Functional Systems” and began the final phase of my doctoral research.
updates.detail: I successfully defended my doctoral proposal, “Transforming Optimized Static Trusses into Shape-morphing Functional Systems.” The defense formalized my research plan for converting optimized static truss designs into adaptive, deployable structures.

updates.title: Graduate student instructor for Introduction to Adaptable & Deployable Structures class
updates.excerpt: I served as a Graduate Student Instructor for the first offering of ENG 100: Introduction to Adaptable and Deployable Structures at the University of Michigan.
updates.detail: I served as a Graduate Student Instructor for the inaugural offering of ENG 100: Introduction to Adaptable and Deployable Structures at the University of Michigan. I guided students through kinematics, rapid prototyping, and analysis fundamentals for morphing systems.

updates.title: Talk at the International Mechanical Engineering Congress and Exposition (IMECE) 2022
updates.excerpt: I was a finalist in the student poster competition at ASME’s IMECE 2022 in Columbus, Ohio, presenting “Adaptable Hull Hydrodynamics using Shape Morphing Curved-Crease Origami.”
updates.detail: I was a finalist in the student poster competition at ASME’s International Mechanical Engineering Congress and Exposition (IMECE) 2022, held in Columbus, Ohio. My poster, “Adaptable Hull Hydrodynamics using Shape Morphing Curved-Crease Origami,” highlighted adaptive marine structures inspired by origami geometry.

updates.title: Talk at the Engineering Mechanics Institute Conference (EMIC) 2022
updates.excerpt: I presented “Hydrodynamic Characteristics of Shape Morphing Curved-Crease Origami Surfaces” at ASCE’s Engineering Mechanics Institute Conference (EMIC) 2022 in Baltimore, Maryland.
updates.detail: At ASCE’s Engineering Mechanics Institute Conference (EMIC) 2022, held in Baltimore, Maryland, I presented “Hydrodynamic Characteristics of Shape Morphing Curved-Crease Origami Surfaces.” The talk detailed experimental and numerical insights into tunable hydrodynamic behavior.

updates.title: Michigan Institute of Computational Discovery and Engineering fellowship
updates.excerpt: I received the Michigan Institute for Computational Discovery and Engineering (MICDE) fellowship and began joint doctoral studies in Civil (Structural) Engineering and Scientific Computing at the University of Michigan.
updates.detail: I was awarded the Michigan Institute for Computational Discovery and Engineering (MICDE) fellowship and began joint doctoral studies in Civil (Structural) Engineering and Scientific Computing at the University of Michigan, focusing on adaptable structural systems.

updates.title: M.S.E. in Structural Engineering, University of Michigan
updates.excerpt: I graduated with a Master of Science in Engineering (MSE) degree in Civil (Structural) Engineering from the University of Michigan with a 4.0 GPA.
updates.detail: I graduated with a Master of Science in Engineering (MSE) in Civil (Structural) Engineering from the University of Michigan, earning a 4.0 GPA while developing my research on deployable structures.

updates.detail: I completed my Bachelor of Technology (B. Tech.) with Honors in Civil Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, graduating with a GPA of 8.5/10 and setting the foundation for my research in adaptable structures.
